beaches.name: Sandy Hook
beaches.area: Gateway National Recreation Area · Monmouth County
beaches.waveNote: Usually moderate in summer; rougher in storms
beaches.entryNote: Beach parking fee, charged 8 a.m.–6 p.m. from Memorial Day weekend to Labor Day. Season pass $100. Cashless: cards or contactless only. Free for military members and veterans with an America the Beautiful pass.
beaches.parking: Several large beach lots. On hot summer weekends they fill up and the park can close the entrance until spaces open, so arrive early.
beaches.description: A seven-mile barrier spit at the top of the Jersey Shore, with wide ocean beaches, dunes, the 1764 Sandy Hook Lighthouse and views of the New York skyline across the bay.
features: Restrooms & showers at the beach areas
beaches.safety: Swim only at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents. Some beaches are a long walk from the lot, so bring water and shade.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Asbury Park
beaches.waveNote: Small summer waves; bigger with fall swells
beaches.entryNote: $10 on weekends and holidays. Season badge $70 for adults, $20 for teens and seniors. Badges aren’t needed after Labor Day.
beaches.parking: Metered street parking and paid lots near the boardwalk, paid by app or kiosk. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A lively mile-long boardwalk with the historic Convention Hall and Paramount Theatre, restaurants and bars right by the sand, and a designated surfing beach.
beaches.safety: Swim only between the lifeguard flags. Surfing is limited to the marked surfing beaches.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Point Pleasant Beach
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.entryNote: Jenkinson’s Beach: $15 on weekends and holidays, and kids under 12 get in free with an adult. Season badge $130 for adults. Buy daily admission at any open beach gate.
beaches.parking: Paid lots and metered street parking near the boardwalk. Lots fill early on summer weekends.
beaches.description: Home of Jenkinson’s Boardwalk, with rides, arcades, an aquarium, mini golf and boardwalk food right behind the sand.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches, and keep an eye on kids in the busy boardwalk crowds.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Seaside Heights
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.entryNote: Kids under 12 free. Weekly badge $50, season badge $75 ($15 for seniors).
beaches.parking: Metered streets and private lots. Lots fill on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A loud, bright boardwalk town with Casino Pier’s rides over the ocean, arcades and pizza stands, and a wide beach in front of it all.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches only. The boardwalk gets very crowded on summer nights.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Island Beach State Park
beaches.waveNote: Open ocean; rougher on windy days
beaches.lifeguardNote: At the ocean swimming areas in summer
beaches.entryNote: Summer weekend rate for New Jersey cars; out-of-state cars pay $20. Weekdays cost less, and the NJ State Parks annual pass ($50) also works. Rates vary by season, so check the park’s site.
beaches.parking: Lots along the park road. On hot summer weekends the park closes the gate once it’s full, so arrive early.
beaches.description: About ten miles of undeveloped barrier island, with dunes, maritime forest and almost no buildings. It’s one of the last natural stretches of the Jersey Shore.
features: Bring your own food and water
beaches.safety: Swim only at the guarded areas, and use the marked paths over the dunes.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Beach Haven
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.entryNote: Weekly badge $20, season badge $50 ($40 if bought before May 31).
beaches.parking: Mostly street parking in town. It gets tight near the beach on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A classic Long Beach Island town with wide guarded beaches, a small-town center of shops and ice cream, and the Fantasy Island amusement park a few blocks from the sand.
features: Shops, ice cream & food in town
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents, especially after storms.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Atlantic City
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.lifeguardNote: Atlantic City Beach Patrol, summer daytime
beaches.entryNote: No beach badge needed.
beaches.parking: Casino garages and paid lots along the boardwalk, plus metered street parking.
beaches.description: Miles of free beach in front of America’s first boardwalk (1870), lined with casinos, Steel Pier rides, shops and food.
beaches.safety: Swim only at guarded beaches, between the lifeguard flags.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Ocean City
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.entryNote: Weekly badge $20, season badge $35 ($30 before June 1). Kids 11 and under are free.
beaches.parking: Metered streets and lots near the boardwalk. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: A dry town (no alcohol sales) with a 2.5-mile boardwalk of rides, mini golf, fudge and pizza, and wide guarded beaches.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches. Surfing is only allowed at the marked surfing beaches.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Wildwood
beaches.waveNote: Gentle on most summer days
beaches.lifeguardNote: Guarded beaches about 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. in summer
beaches.entryNote: No beach tags in Wildwood, North Wildwood or Wildwood Crest.
beaches.parking: Metered streets and private lots near the boardwalk.
beaches.description: One of the widest beaches on the East Coast, with a long walk to the water, Morey’s Piers rides and waterparks, and the boardwalk tram car.
beaches.safety: Swimming is only allowed at guarded beaches. The sand is wide and hot, so bring shoes.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Cape May
beaches.waveNote: Usually gentle in summer
beaches.entryNote: Season badge $40.
beaches.parking: Metered street parking and lots near the beach. It fills up on summer weekends.
beaches.description: The southern tip of New Jersey, with Victorian streets, a beachfront promenade, dolphin-watching boat trips and Cape May Lighthouse nearby.
beaches.safety: Swim at guarded beaches and watch for rip currents near the jetties.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Siesta Key Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually gentle Gulf water
beaches.lifeguardNote: Four lifeguard stations; hours vary by season
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: About 950 free spaces. They fill quickly in peak season (January–April), so arrive early or take the free trolley.
beaches.description: A wide beach of bright white, powder-soft quartz sand with gentle Gulf water, regularly named one of the best beaches in America.
beaches.safety: Swim near a lifeguard station and watch for rip current warnings on windy days.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Clearwater Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually calm Gulf water
beaches.lifeguardNote: 10 a.m.–5 p.m. daily; towers staffed by season and weather
beaches.entryNote: Public beach.
beaches.parking: Paid city lots and garages near Pier 60. Rates vary by lot, so check the meter. Lots fill on weekends.
beaches.description: Wide, soft white sand on the Gulf, calm water and beachfront restaurants, with Pier 60 at the center for watching the sunset.
beaches.safety: Swim near a staffed lifeguard tower. Parts of Pier 60 may be closed after storm damage, so check before you go.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: South Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually gentle; rougher with winter fronts
beaches.lifeguardNote: Miami Beach Ocean Rescue towers staffed daily; check posted hours
beaches.entryNote: Public beach.
beaches.parking: Paid garages and metered street parking. Rates rise on busy and event weekends, and spaces near the beach fill fast.
beaches.hours: Lummus Park is open sunrise to midnight.
beaches.description: Miami’s famous city beach: wide sand and blue-green water in front of the pastel Art Deco hotels of Ocean Drive.
features: Art Deco buildings along Ocean Drive
beaches.safety: Swim near a staffed lifeguard tower and check the warning flags before going in.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Bahia Honda State Park
beaches.waveNote: Shallow and usually calm
beaches.lifeguardNote: No lifeguards; swim at your own risk
beaches.entryNote: For 2–8 people, plus a 50¢ per person Monroe County surcharge. Single-person vehicles $4.50; walk-ins and cyclists $2.50.
beaches.parking: Parking inside the park is included with entry. It can fill on busy days.
beaches.description: A Florida Keys state park with clear, shallow turquoise water, three beaches on the Atlantic and Florida Bay, and views of the old Bahia Honda Rail Bridge.
features: Views of the old Bahia Honda Rail Bridge
beaches.safety: There are no lifeguards. Stay away from the Bahia Honda Channel, where the currents are very strong.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Daytona Beach
beaches.waveNote: Atlantic surf; bigger with storms
beaches.lifeguardNote: Volusia County Beach Safety towers; staffing varies, check the Volusia Beaches app
beaches.entryNote: Free to walk on. Driving and parking on the sand need a pass, with different prices for residents and visitors; check Park Volusia for current rates.
beaches.parking: Drive-on beach sections (when the tide allows) and off-beach lots, both paid.
beaches.description: A wide, hard-packed beach where you can still drive and park on the sand in some sections, with the boardwalk and Main Street Pier at its center.
beaches.safety: Watch for cars on the drive-on sections and swim near a staffed lifeguard tower; rip currents are common.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Waikīkī Beach
beaches.waveNote: Gentle rollers; bigger south swells in summer
beaches.entryNote: Public beach, open to everyone.
beaches.parking: Scarce and metered. Use a hotel or shopping garage or the Fort DeRussy lot; most visitors walk from their hotel.
beaches.description: About two miles of golden sand in front of Diamond Head, with soft rolling waves where beginner surf lessons happen right off the sand. Busy, buzzy and in the heart of Honolulu.
features: Restrooms & showers at Kūhiō Beach Park
beaches.safety: The water is crowded. Watch for surfers and outrigger canoes in the lesson areas.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Hanauma Bay
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered by a reef inside an old volcanic crater
beaches.entryNote: For non-residents, plus an online fee. Free for Hawaiʻi residents, kids 12 and under, and active military. Non-residents need a reservation, released 2 days ahead at 7 a.m. HST.
beaches.parking: $3 for non-residents, $1 for residents. Cash only, first come first served, even with a reservation.
beaches.description: A protected nature preserve in a volcanic crater, with clear, calm water over coral reef. It’s Oʻahu’s best-known place to snorkel with reef fish and turtles.
beaches.safety: Don’t stand on the coral or touch turtles. Book your entry two days ahead.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Lanikai Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually calm, reef-protected water
beaches.entryNote: Reached by public paths between homes.
beaches.parking: No lot, and street parking is very limited and strictly enforced. Park at Kailua Beach Park and walk.
beaches.description: A slim ribbon of powder-soft sand facing the twin Mokulua islets. It’s often called the most beautiful beach in Hawaiʻi, and it was No. 9 on Dr. Beach’s 2025 list of top US beaches.
beaches.safety: There are no lifeguards or facilities. Park legally and use the marked public paths.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Waimea Bay
beaches.waveNote: Glassy in summer; winter waves can top 20 ft
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: Free lot. It fills very early on weekends and big-surf days.
beaches.description: A deep, sandy bay that’s calm enough to swim and snorkel in summer and home to giant surf in winter. The famous jump rock sits at the south end.
beaches.safety: Winter surf and currents are deadly. Swim roughly May–Sept, and only jump from the rock when it’s calm and the lifeguards say so.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Kailua Beach Park
beaches.waveNote: Gentle, with steady trade winds
beaches.entryNote: Public beach park.
beaches.parking: Big free lot.
beaches.description: Wide, soft sand and turquoise water on Kailua Bay, with an easy kayak launch toward the offshore islets and steady breezes for windsurfers and kiteboarders.
beaches.safety: Trade winds can push kayaks and boards offshore. Check the wind before you paddle out.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Santa Monica
beaches.waveNote: Gentle surf most days; bigger swells in winter
beaches.lifeguardNote: LA County lifeguards all year, with more towers staffed in summer
beaches.entryNote: A public state beach, open to everyone.
beaches.parking: Paid beach lots and metered street parking. Prices go up on summer weekends; the Metro E Line ends a few blocks away.
beaches.description: A wide, sandy city beach next to Santa Monica Pier, with its Ferris wheel and arcade, and a beach bike path that runs south to Venice.
beaches.safety: Swim near a staffed lifeguard tower and away from the pier pilings. Skip swimming for a few days after heavy rain (runoff).
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: La Jolla Cove
beaches.waveNote: Small, sheltered cove; calmest in summer and early fall
beaches.lifeguardNote: City lifeguards watch the cove from a tower on the cliff
beaches.entryNote: Free and open to the public.
beaches.parking: Limited free street parking that fills early; paid lots in La Jolla village.
beaches.description: A tiny sandy cove below sandstone cliffs, inside a protected marine reserve: clear water for snorkeling with bright orange garibaldi fish, and sea lions and seals on the rocks nearby.
beaches.safety: Give sea lions and seals lots of space. Nothing may be taken from the reserve. The cove gets rough when big swells arrive.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Huntington Beach
beaches.waveNote: Consistent surf, especially around the pier
beaches.lifeguardNote: City and state lifeguards all year, with more towers in summer
beaches.entryNote: Free and open to the public.
beaches.parking: Metered street parking and paid beach lots along Pacific Coast Highway.
beaches.description: Miles of wide sand around a long wooden pier, with steady surf, beach fire rings, a bike path and Main Street's shops and restaurants right behind the beach.
beaches.safety: Swim between lifeguard towers and well away from the pier. Watch for rip currents and surfers.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Grace Bay
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered by a barrier reef offshore
beaches.lifeguardNote: No lifeguards on most of the beach
beaches.entryNote: All beaches in the Turks and Caicos are public.
beaches.parking: Free public access paths along the beach, some with small parking areas.
beaches.description: A long, soft white-sand beach with very calm, clear turquoise water, sheltered by a barrier reef. Snorkel the reef at Bight Reef (Coral Gardens) at the western end.
beaches.safety: There are no lifeguards. Don't stand on or touch the coral, and use reef-safe sunscreen.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Seven Mile Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually calm on Grand Cayman's sheltered west side
beaches.lifeguardNote: No lifeguards on most of the beach
beaches.entryNote: Free. Public Beach and Governor's Beach are easy public access points.
beaches.parking: Free parking at Public Beach and Governor's Beach.
beaches.description: A long curve of soft white coral sand along Grand Cayman's calm west coast, lined with hotels and beach bars. Snorkel the reef off Cemetery Beach at the north end.
beaches.safety: No lifeguards. Watch for boats and jet skis offshore; swim close to the beach.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Eagle Beach
beaches.waveNote: Usually gentle on Aruba's sheltered west coast
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Free parking along the road behind the beach.
beaches.description: One of the widest beaches in the Caribbean, with powdery white sand, calm water and Aruba's famous wind-bent fofoti trees. Sea turtles nest here in season.
beaches.safety: No lifeguards. Stay clear of marked turtle nests.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Tulum Beach
beaches.waveNote: Small waves; the reef offshore softens the swell
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguards at some public beaches; many stretches have none
beaches.entryNote: Some beach entrances, including those inside the national park around the ruins, charge an entry fee. Check current prices locally.
beaches.parking: Paid lots near the ruins and the beach clubs.
beaches.description: Powdery white sand and turquoise water below Tulum's clifftop Maya ruins, with laid-back beach clubs stretching south along the coast.
beaches.safety: Seaweed (sargassum) can pile up in spring and summer, so check conditions before you go. Swim only where it's calm.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Bávaro Beach
beaches.waveNote: A reef offshore keeps it fairly gentle
beaches.lifeguardNote: Some resort stretches have lifeguards; check the flags
beaches.entryNote: Beaches in the Dominican Republic are public.
beaches.parking: Little public parking; most visitors come from nearby resorts or by taxi.
beaches.description: A long stretch of soft white sand lined with coconut palms and resorts on the Dominican Republic's east coast.
beaches.safety: Follow the beach flags, and swim near lifeguards where there are some.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Copacabana
beaches.waveNote: Open Atlantic beach; waves and currents can be strong
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguard posts (postos) all along the beach
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Street parking is scarce; take the metro to Cardeal Arcoverde, Siqueira Campos or Cantagalo.
beaches.description: Rio's famous 2.5-mile beach curving along Avenida Atlântica, with its wave-pattern promenade, beach kiosks, volleyball and views of Sugarloaf Mountain.
beaches.safety: Bring only what you need and keep valuables close. Swim near a lifeguard post and follow the flags.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Ipanema
beaches.waveNote: Stronger waves, especially at the Arpoador end
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Very little parking; the metro stops at General Osório and Nossa Senhora da Paz.
beaches.description: A lively, stylish beach between the Arpoador rocks and the twin peaks of Dois Irmãos. At sunset, crowds on Arpoador rock clap as the sun goes down.
beaches.safety: Waves and rip currents can be strong: swim near a lifeguard post. Keep valuables out of sight.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Baía do Sancho
beaches.waveNote: Calmest from about April to November; big swells can arrive from December to March
beaches.entryNote: Every visitor to Fernando de Noronha pays a daily environmental fee, and Sancho is inside the marine national park, which needs its own ticket. Daily visitor numbers are limited.
beaches.parking: No cars at the beach: get to the trailhead by buggy, bus or taxi, then climb down ladders through the cliff (or arrive by boat).
beaches.description: A small cove of golden sand below green cliffs in Fernando de Noronha's marine national park, often voted one of the best beaches in the world. Clear water, sea turtles and reef fish.
beaches.safety: The way down is steep ladders inside a crack in the cliff. There are no lifeguards; ask park staff about sea conditions.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Praia da Marinha
beaches.waveNote: Usually calm in summer on the sheltered south coast
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguards during the official bathing season (roughly June to September)
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Free car park at the top of the cliff; it fills by late morning in summer.
beaches.description: Golden sand framed by tall limestone cliffs, sea arches and caves. The cliff-top Seven Hanging Valleys trail runs east toward Benagil.
beaches.safety: Keep away from the base of the cliffs (falling rocks). The path down is steep.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Praia do Camilo
beaches.waveNote: Small, sheltered cove
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguards during the official bathing season
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Small car park at the top; Lagos town is about a 30-minute walk.
beaches.description: A small cove of golden sand reached by a long wooden staircase down the cliffs, with clear water and rock formations near Ponta da Piedade.
beaches.safety: It's about 200 steps each way. The beach is small and shrinks a lot at high tide.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: La Concha
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered by the bay and Santa Clara island
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Paid underground car parks in the city center.
beaches.description: A shell-shaped city beach on a sheltered bay, with an elegant promenade and its famous white railing, Santa Clara island in the middle of the bay, and the old town's pintxos bars a short walk away.
beaches.safety: The water is cool even in summer, around 68–72°F.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Navagio (Shipwreck Beach)
beaches.waveNote: Calm in summer; boats don't run in rough weather
beaches.entryNote: Reachable only by boat. Because of rockfall risk, boats have often not been allowed to land in recent years, so many trips only view it from the water. Check the latest rules before you book.
beaches.parking: Parking near the cliff-top viewpoint above the cove.
beaches.description: A white-pebble cove with a rusting shipwreck, enclosed by towering limestone cliffs and bright blue water: one of the most photographed places in Greece.
beaches.safety: Rockfall risk: follow any landing ban and keep away from the cliffs.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Elafonissi
beaches.waveNote: A shallow, warm lagoon
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguards on the main beach in summer; check locally
beaches.entryNote: Free. The area is a protected nature reserve.
beaches.parking: Paid parking near the beach in summer.
beaches.description: A shallow turquoise lagoon and sandbar with pink-tinted sand (from crushed shells), in a protected nature area at Crete's southwest tip.
beaches.safety: Don't take any sand or shells: the area is protected. There's little natural shade.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Myrtos
beaches.waveNote: Deep water close to shore; waves when the wind blows from the west
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Free car park at the bottom of a steep, winding road.
beaches.description: A long curve of white pebbles below green cliffs, with unusually bright blue water. The view from the road above is one of the most famous in the Ionian Islands.
beaches.safety: The water gets deep quickly and the pebbles shift underfoot; take care with kids.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Rabbit Beach
beaches.waveNote: A sheltered cove with shallow, clear water
beaches.entryNote: Free, inside a nature reserve. In summer, visitor numbers are limited and you may need a free booking. It's closed at night because turtles nest here.
beaches.parking: Small car park at the top, then a 10–15 minute walk down a path.
beaches.description: A small white-sand cove facing Rabbit Island (Spiaggia dei Conigli), with very clear, shallow water. Loggerhead sea turtles nest here in summer.
beaches.safety: Follow the reserve rules: some areas are closed for turtle nests. Bring water and shade.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Maya Bay
beaches.waveNote: An enclosed bay ringed by cliffs
beaches.lifeguardNote: Park rangers patrol; swimming isn't allowed
beaches.entryNote: Inside a national park that charges foreign visitors an entry fee. You arrive on a boat tour; boats dock at the back of the island and you walk in on a boardwalk.
beaches.parking: No cars: boat tours leave from Phi Phi Don, Phuket and Krabi.
beaches.hours: Closed every year from about August to September so the bay can recover.
beaches.description: The cliff-ringed bay made famous by the film The Beach. It closed for years so the coral could recover, and now has strict limits: you can walk on the sand, but swimming isn't allowed.
features: Blacktip reef sharks in the bay
beaches.safety: No swimming. Stay on the boardwalk and marked areas.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Railay West
beaches.waveNote: Calm most of the year; rougher in the monsoon (about May–October)
beaches.entryNote: Free. Railay can only be reached by longtail boat, from Ao Nang or Krabi town.
beaches.parking: No cars: park in Ao Nang and take a longtail boat.
beaches.description: A crescent of soft sand between giant limestone cliffs, reachable only by boat. World-famous for rock climbing, with sunsets over the Andaman Sea.
beaches.safety: No lifeguards. Watch for longtail boats near the shore.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Kuta Beach
beaches.waveNote: A sandy-bottom beach break, popular for surf lessons
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguards with towers and flags along the main stretch
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Paid car and scooter parking near the beach; traffic is heavy.
beaches.description: Bali's best-known surf beach: a long stretch of sand with friendly beach-break waves for beginners, board rentals everywhere and famous sunsets.
beaches.safety: Swim between the red-and-yellow flags: rip currents are common. Rubbish washes up in the wet season (about November to March).
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: White Beach
beaches.waveNote: Calm in the dry season; choppier during the southwest monsoon (about June–September)
beaches.lifeguardNote: Lifeguard stations along the beach; check locally
beaches.entryNote: Visitors to Boracay pay an environmental fee and a port terminal fee, and need a booking at an accredited hotel.
beaches.parking: No car needed: arrive by boat from Caticlan and get around by e-trike.
beaches.description: Four kilometers of powder-soft white sand with calm, shallow water, famous for sunset sailing on traditional paraw boats.
features: Restaurants & bars on the beach path
beaches.safety: Follow the beach flags. Don't drink or smoke on the sand: Boracay has strict beach rules.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Bondi Beach
beaches.waveNote: Open surf beach; usually bigger at the south end
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Paid street and lot parking; buses from Bondi Junction station are easier.
beaches.description: Sydney's most famous beach: a golden crescent of surf, the Bondi Icebergs ocean pool and the start of the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk.
beaches.safety: Always swim between the red-and-yellow flags: Bondi has strong rip currents.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Manly Beach
beaches.waveNote: Surf on the main beach; calm water at Shelly Beach around the corner
beaches.entryNote: Free. The ferry from Circular Quay is the classic way to get there.
beaches.parking: Paid parking near the beach; the ferry is easier.
beaches.description: A lively surf beach lined with Norfolk pines, a 30-minute ferry ride from central Sydney. Walk around to Shelly Beach, a protected cove for snorkeling with big blue groper fish.
beaches.safety: Swim between the flags.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Whitehaven Beach
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered, with small waves
beaches.lifeguardNote: No lifeguards: it's inside a national park
beaches.entryNote: No road access: visit on a day trip by boat, seaplane or helicopter from Airlie Beach or Hamilton Island. Tour prices vary.
beaches.parking: No cars: tours leave from Airlie Beach and Hamilton Island.
beaches.description: Seven kilometers of brilliant white, almost pure silica sand in Whitsunday Islands National Park. From the Hill Inlet lookout, sand and water swirl together at low tide.
beaches.safety: Marine stingers (box jellyfish) are around from about November to May, so wear a stinger suit. Bring water and sun protection.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Byron Bay
beaches.waveNote: Gentle surf at Main Beach; bigger waves at The Pass and beyond
beaches.lifeguardNote: Patrolled by lifeguards; check the flag times
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Paid parking near the beach; it fills quickly.
beaches.description: A relaxed surf-town beach below Cape Byron lighthouse, mainland Australia's most easterly point. Dolphins are common, and humpback whales pass by in winter and spring.
beaches.safety: Swim between the flags. Watch for rip currents, especially after big swells.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Anse Source d'Argent
beaches.waveNote: Protected by a reef; very shallow at low tide
beaches.entryNote: You reach it through L'Union Estate, which charges an entry fee (the estate also has giant tortoises and an old plantation).
beaches.parking: No cars on La Digue: cycle or walk from La Passe.
beaches.description: Pink-tinted granite boulders, powdery sand and shallow turquoise water: one of the most photographed beaches in the world.
beaches.safety: The water gets very shallow at low tide; go near high tide for swimming. No lifeguards.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Anse Lazio
beaches.waveNote: Usually calm; rougher during the southeast trade winds (about May–September)
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Small free car park at the beach.
beaches.description: A wide bay of white sand framed by granite rocks and takamaka trees, with clear water and snorkeling around the rocks at either end.
beaches.safety: No lifeguards. Swim in the calm middle of the bay and watch for currents near the rocks.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Camps Bay
beaches.waveNote: Atlantic waves; can be strong
beaches.entryNote: Free and public.
beaches.parking: Paid street parking along Victoria Road; busy on summer weekends.
beaches.description: White sand and palm trees below the Twelve Apostles mountains, with cafés and restaurants just across the road. The Atlantic water is cold even in summer.
beaches.safety: The water is cold (often 55–60°F) and currents can be strong. Swim only where lifeguards are on duty.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).

beaches.name: Boulders Beach
beaches.waveNote: Sheltered by huge granite boulders
beaches.entryNote: Part of Table Mountain National Park: a conservation fee is charged (lower for South African residents).
beaches.parking: Paid parking near the entrances.
beaches.hours: Opening hours change with the season; check before you go.
beaches.description: A sheltered cove of granite boulders and calm water, home to a colony of endangered African penguins. Boardwalks let you watch them up close.
beaches.safety: Don't touch or feed the penguins: they can bite.
beaches.monthlySource: Averages of daily data: air and rain 2016–2025, waves and water 2016–2025. Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0).
